# Setup
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dpi = 300, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

library(rtracklayer)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(Biostrings)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

genomedir <- here("species/crob/KY21")
```

# Data
```{r}
protfa <- readAAStringSet(here(genomedir, "data/ghost-db/HT.KY21Gene.protein.2.fasta.gz"))

read_gxf_as_tibble <- function(.file) {
  rtracklayer::import(.file) %>% 
    GenomicRanges::as.data.frame() %>% 
    as_tibble()
} 

gtf <- read_gxf_as_tibble(here(genomedir, "results/gtf/ky21_fixed.gtf.gz"))
ens_pfa <- readAAStringSet("https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-113/fasta/ciona_intestinalis/pep/Ciona_intestinalis.KH.pep.all.fa.gz")
```

## Remove proteins missing from the GTF
There are ~300 proteins that are present in the proteome fasta from ghostdb but are missing from the GTF. For consistency, we will remove them from the fasta file. 

```{r}
gtf_pids <- unique(gtf$protein_id[which(!is.na(gtf$protein_id))])

names(protfa)[!names(protfa) %in% gtf_pids]
```

```{r}
protfa <- protfa[names(protfa) %in% gtf_pids]
```

```{r}
stopifnot(all(names(protfa) %in% gtf_pids))
stopifnot(all(gtf_pids[!grepl("ENSCINP", gtf_pids)] %in% names(protfa)))
```

## Strip non-methionine AA at the beginning

The protein FASTA from GHOSTdb is translation of the longest ORF, so it doesn't always start with methionine. We need to strip the amino acids before the first M in all protein sequences. 

> This file contains translated sequences of the longest ORFs; They do not always begin with Methionine; Remove amino acids prior to the first Methionine if you need.

```{r}
strip_to_first_met <- function(x) {
  gsub("([^M]*?)(M.*)", "\\2", x)
}

protfa_met <- protfa

pb <- txtProgressBar(min = 1, max = length(protfa_met), style = 3)
for (i in seq_along(protfa_met)) {
  protfa_met[[i]] <- strip_to_first_met(protfa_met[[i]])
  setTxtProgressBar(pb, i)
}
close(pb)
```

# Tests

## Are all sequences now shorter (or the same length) than before?

```{r}
plot(width(protfa), width(protfa_met))
```


```{r}
hist(width(protfa) - width(protfa_met))
summary(width(protfa) - width(protfa_met))
```

## Do all sequences now start with methionine?

There are 987 sequences that don't start with an MET, because they don't have a methionine in the sequence at all. 

```{r}
protfa_met[!grepl("^M", protfa_met)]
```

We will still keep them around. 

# Append mitochondrial proteins

```{r}
mt_protein_ids <- gtf %>% 
  filter(seqnames == "MT") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(protein_id)) %>% 
  pull(protein_id) %>%
  unique()

strip_fasta_description <- function(x) {
  str_replace(x, "(.+?)\\s.*", "\\1")
}

remove_id_version <- function(x) {
  str_replace(x, "(ENSCINP\\d+)\\.\\d+", "\\1")
}

names(ens_pfa) <- names(ens_pfa) %>% 
  strip_fasta_description() %>% 
  remove_id_version()

mt_pfa <- ens_pfa[mt_protein_ids]

protfa_met_with_mt <- c(mt_pfa, protfa_met)
```


# Write files

```{r}
writeXStringSet(protfa_met_with_mt, 
                here(genomedir, 
                     "results/fasta/KY21_proteins_met_with-mito.fasta.gz"), 
                format = "fasta", 
                compress = "gzip")
```
